name: Amon
author: Paul Overy

provenance.from: kyzer.me.uk/amos/other/amon-v1.03.lha, retrieved 2026-08-12 and held in the corpus at sources/kyzer-amon/. Stuart Caie's AMOS extension archive -- "old archives go offline, so now I maintain my own archives of them". The package carries the library twice, identically, once for AMOS Classic and once for AMOS Pro; this is the APSystem copy.
provenance.note: The earlier release, and a separate identity: two of the eighteen keyword ids move between it and 1.04. Never held as a stub -- the AMOSTools collection's "V1.03" file is 1.04's table.
provenance.redistribution: Shareware: free under the interpreter, GBP 5 to the author for use in compiled code. Not redistributed by amos-ts; fixtures/ is gitignored.

findings: The 18-keyword release. Six keywords fewer than 1.04: Fast Point, Array Plot, Joy3, Joy4, Count Colour and Find Colour arrive later. Registered as its own identity because two shared ids MOVED -- `test add` 306 -> 374 and `fast circle` 330 -> 326 -- so neither table can stand in for the other and a 1.03 program calling Test Add holds an id meaning Fast Point in 1.04. That is the `renumbered` verdict src/cli/versweep.ts refuses to auto-bind, and this is the first real pair it has had to judge. DEFECT: THE MANUAL AND THE BINARY DISAGREE ABOUT THE SLOT, BY ONE. `Amon1.3.doc` says "Enter the name of the new extension in slot 15"; the library says 16, twice -- routine 0 stores its base to `$1e8(a5)`, and `$f8 + (16-1)*16` IS $1e8, then returns `moveq #$f,d0`, the extension number zero-based. A user who follows the manual installs it at 15, whereupon the library publishes its base into slot 16's entry and leaves its own null: it corrupts a neighbour and cannot find its own data. 1.04 moved to slot 25 and its manual agrees with its binary, which is plausibly why the move happened. ExoticA's extensions wiki lists AMon at 15, which is where the registered stub's slot came from -- the wiki took the 1.03 manual's number, and it is wrong for both releases. `recommendedSlot` here is 16, the binary's, because a slot the library cannot actually work in is not a recommendation.
